questions.question: In the initial presentation, how did the clinical picture of DIC and sepsis complicate the diagnosis of the subsequent Thrombotic Microangiopathy, and why is the timing of hemolysis significant?
What specific laboratory finding definitively excludes Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) as a diagnosis of exclusion in a patient presenting with Thrombotic Microangiopathy?
The patient tested negative for Shiga toxin and lacked bowel symptoms; what specific criteria support the exclusion of STEC-HUS in favor of an infection-triggered CM-HUS diagnosis?
What is the pathophysiological mechanism proposing that Capnocytophaga canimorsus bacteremia can directly trigger endothelial injury in the absence of a genetic complement variant?
Why do conventional serum complement levels (C3/C4) fail to rule out complement-mediated HUS during the acute active phase, and how does the functional assay (alternative pathway) clarify this?
Why was Plasma Exchange (PEX) used as a bridging therapy rather than a definitive treatment, and what is the therapeutic limitation of PEX in this specific context compared to eculizumab?

What critical precautions regarding vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis are required to mitigate the risks of invasive infection associated with eculizumab therapy in a patient with a severe bacterial infection?
Based on the study outcomes, what factor is more predictive of favorable renal recovery than long-term eculizumab maintenance alone: time to initiation of therapy or continuation duration?
